channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Trust ‘unaware’ of critical review when it hired new chief
item.description: A trust which hired the boss of Wales’s biggest health board as its new CEO said it was “unaware” of the findings of a critical review into the board’s leadership during her tenure when it made the appointment.

item.title: Few boards acting on race inequalities in maternity care
item.description: Few trust boards are reviewing and acting on variation in maternity outcomes by ethnicity and deprivation, NHS England’s chief nursing officer has warned.

item.title: Hospital forced to halt ‘gas and air’ after years of warnings
item.description: A major trust has halted the use of gas and air at one of its hospitals after declaring staff exposure was “above acceptable levels”, prompting the midwives’ union to accuse it of “putting staff safety and patient care into conflict”.

item.title: Mackey to leave NHSE by April
item.description: Sir Jim Mackey will leave as NHS chief executive no later than the end of March, NHS England’s chair has said – but the government is holding up recruitment of his successor.

item.title: NHSE must move ‘very quickly’ to replace FDP, warns director
item.description: The NHS must no longer be dependent “on any one supplier” to provide the federated data platform, according to the chair of the NHS England data, digital and technology committee.

item.title: Trust discriminated against surgeon it rated ‘appointable’
item.description: A trust racially discriminated against an orthopaedic surgeon by not appointing him to a role that he was the only candidate for, an employment tribunal has ruled.

item.title: NHS now has 36 staff for every manager
item.description: The growth in the number of NHS managers has been nearly five times less that of other staff groups in the past 16 years, according to new analysis shared with HSJ .

item.title: DHSC ‘may well’ force trusts to cede spending powers
item.description: NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care are pressing ahead with a centralisation of authority over NHS procurement services, and have not ruled out making trust involvement mandatory.

item.title: NHS on course to miss flu jab target despite improved uptake
item.description: More NHS staff have been vaccinated against flu than at this time last year, but the service is still likely to fall well short of the target set by NHS England.

item.title: Neighbourhood contracts paused after NHSE warning
item.description: An integrated care board has paused plans to delegate responsibility for commissioning out-of-hospital services to a lead provider in each part of its patch.

item.title: Speak Up Guardian claims she was silenced by top trust’s leaders
item.description: An “outstanding”-rated trust is contesting an unfair dismissal claim from its former Freedom to Speak Up Guardian, who claims she was punished for raising concerns with senior leaders.

item.title: Winners of the 2026 HSJ Awards revealed
item.description: The winners of the 2026 HSJ Awards were announced last night.

item.title: Former national director to chair trust
item.description: A former Health Education England medical director has been appointed to chair a specialist acute trust.

item.title: Consultancy wins £41m single patient record deal
item.description: NHS England has awarded a £41m contract to a big four consultancy firm to support a range of major technology initiatives.

item.title: Revealed: The trust where 40% of A&E patients end up in a corridor
item.description: The number of patients in corridors represents around a quarter of A&E attendances at some trusts – with the ratio rising to nearly 40 per cent at one major teaching hospital – figures suggest.

item.title: ‘Overly complex’ £22m procurement ‘must be abandoned’
item.description: A trust has been told to abandon an “overly complex” £22m procurement for renal services after being found to have breached 16 Provider Selection Regime regulations.

item.title: Trust ‘faces £3m payout’ after whistleblower ruling
item.description: A teaching hospital trust could face a potential £3m payout to a whistleblower who accused “senior people” at the trust of concealing information relating to deaths, patient mistreatment and sexual assaults, after a tribunal threw out its defence to her unfair dismissal case.

item.title: Revealed: One in five pensions paid late
item.description: There were so many delays to NHS pensions over the past 18 months that government had to pay out millions in compensation for lost interest.

item.title: Cooper vows to ‘refocus’ neighbourhood health reform
item.description: The health and social care secretary has pledged to “refocus” neighbourhood health reforms away from “boundaries [and] restructuring”.

item.title: ‘Senior people’ accused of covering up death and sexual assault allegations
item.description: A former head of safeguarding has accused “senior people” at a teaching hospital of concealing information relating to deaths, mistreatment of patients and sexual assaults, a tribunal heard.
